title: Quant intake chaos harness and SLA-focused regression auditor
creator: Aisha Gomez
description:
Summary: Build an automated intake and certification flow for low-precision model artifacts (INT8/GPTQ/AWQ/FP8) that combines a lightweight chaos harness with SLA-focused regression detection. Goal is to give model owners a deterministic pass/fail signal tied to production SLOs and an automated pinning suggestion for safe rollout.

Goals:
- Gate incoming quantized artifacts with a reproducible smoke and stress run that simulates production tail latency and KV-cache churn.
- Compute a single perf-regression score that combines latency, e2e quality delta (task-specific), and token-cost delta.
- Provide deterministic pin recommendation (pin / soft-pin / do-not-pin) and produce a draft version-pin manifest for Console and Dedicated.
- Publish a signed "quant-cert" artifact with metrics, fingerprint, and rollback recipe.

Success criteria:
- New intake flow auto-classifies >80% of submitted variants without manual review within 24h.
- Regression false-positive rate <3% on controlled historical baseline.
- Rollout recommendations integrate with pin registry and Console canary automation.

Design/approach (high level):
1) Intake runner: a containerized task that accepts quant artifacts and runs staged checks: micro-bench (kernel latency), synthetic canary (small prompt set), KV churn stress (long-context traces), and a short quality eval set keyed to the model family. Each stage emits standardized metrics.
2) Chaos harness: while running the micro-bench we inject realistic degradations (GPU load, small memory pressure, slower all-reduce) in a controlled sandbox to surface fragility. We record which degradation mode triggers SLO breach.
3) Regression auditor: lightweight aggregator that normalizes signals into z-scores, applies weights, and computes the perf-regression-score. Thresholds map to pin decisions.
4) Artifact publishing: when pass, create quant-cert JSON (signed) with model fingerprint, quant-profile metadata, telemetry snapshot, and a one-click GitHub PR template to promote to pin registry.

Telemetry signals and thresholds (first-pass):
- quant_latency_p50, quant_latency_p95, quant_latency_p99 (SLO: p95 < baseline*1.15)
- e2e_quality_delta (task-specific; fail if >2.5% absolute drop for NLU tasks)
- token_cost_delta (budget: <= +8% cost)
- fragility_index (counts of degradation modes that cause >SLO violation; fail if >1)
- perf_regression_score (composite, 0-100; fail if >35)

Acceptance criteria for a single artifact:
- All smoke checks pass AND perf_regression_score <= 35 OR
- If score in (36..60) then artifact flagged for manual review and requires geneva-level signoff.
- If score > 60 then reject.

Rollout plan:
Phase A (internal): enable flow for engineering-only artifacts. Integrate with CI; require cert before promoting to staging.
Phase B (hybrid): allow trusted partners to submit artifacts via an upload UI; auto-create draft pin and Slack notify owners.
Phase C (public): integrate with Console and pin registry; UI in Console shows cert and one-click promote.

Edge cases and trade-offs:
- Running full-quality evals is expensive; we rely on small family-specific sets as a proxy. Plan nightly long-run evaluations for overnight stability checks.
- Chaos modes might produce brittle signals for some model families; we will maintain per-family weight overrides in the auditor.
- False positives reduce velocity; thresholds will be calibrated on a labeled historical dataset.

Deliverables:
- Launcher container and runner script (intake-runner:v1)
- Chaos harness module (chaos-sim:v1) with three canned degradation profiles
- Auditor service and scoring library (py) with config-driven weights
- quant-cert artifact schema and signing flow
- Console UI wireframes and API endpoints for draft pin promotion

Open questions:
- How to standardize the small eval sets across community-contributed models? (proposal: curated seed sets per family in a shared git repo)
- Owner signoff flow for soft-pin decisions (suggest Slack + Console task)
